text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday: NEUE ZUERCHER ZEITUNG - Vice president of the Jewish World Congress Greville Janner demanded a re-negotiation of the Washington Treaty between Switzerland and the Allies with regard to Swiss Nazi gold compensation payments. Janner spoke at the Swiss-British Chamber of Commerce in Zurich on Monady. - Professor Hans Schmid of the University of St. Gallen said the Foundation for Solidarity, which Switzerland wants to finance with its gold reserves, might threaten the stability of the Swiss franc. TAGES ANZEIGER - Swiss cable television operator Cablecom plans to introduce high-speed internet access throughout Switzerland, which should be a 100 times faster than ordinary internet connections. Cablecom is a major player in the Swiss cable television market with a share of 50 percent. - Swissair's shares registered a 56 Swiss francs rise to 1,285 francs on Monday. Analysts regared the airlines' 1996 operative results as positive. - Charges at the Swiss Stock Exchange will drop from 15 to 10 centimes for a 1,000 Swiss franc order, starting at the beginning of next year. - ABB Switzerland said it will take over Basle-based electro installation company Kriegel and Schaffner per January 1, 1997. Financial details have not been disclosed. Kriegel and Schaffner has a workforce 650 employees and registered a 1996 turnover of 90 million Swiss francs. JOURNAL DE GENEVE - Swiss homoeopaths frear that they will lose independance as Switzerland's drug control administration plans to introduce a perscription scheme for homoeopathic medication. - Swiss tour operator Hotelplan reported a 1995/96 net profit of 4.2 million Swiss francs, up from 0.2 million francs in the previous fiscal year. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
